chunks: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding the falcon, and the hawk, and the eagle?' So he said, 'If you reach it (while alive) for its slaughter, then eat from it. And if you do not reach it for its slaughter, then do not eat.'

key_terms.الصَّقْرِ: hawk or hunting bird (saqr) — a generic term for birds of prey used in hunting
key_terms.الْبَازِي: falcon (baz) — a trained bird of prey used in falconry
key_terms.الْعُقَابِ: eagle (uqab) — a large bird of prey
key_terms.ذَكَاتَهُ: tadhkiyah — ritual slaughter; the condition making prey lawful for consumption

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Islam to eat prey caught by falcons, hawks, and eagles?
ai.summary: Abu Ubayda al-Hadhdha' asked Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about the permissibility of eating prey caught by birds of prey — specifically the falcon (baz), hawk (saqr), and eagle (uqab). The Imam ruled that if the hunter reaches the prey while it is still alive and performs the ritual slaughter (tadhkiyah), then it is permissible to eat. If the prey is found already dead without slaughter, it is forbidden. This ruling reflects the Islamic jurisprudential principle that game caught by trained birds of prey must be slaughtered by the hunter if found alive, distinguishing this case from game caught by trained hunting dogs which may be eaten even if found dead.
